The coagulation pathway is activated by all hemodialysis membranes and fibrin deposition is the most important factor for the development of membrane-induced complement activation.
the coagulation cascade and the complement system are activated by all membranes, whereas fibrinogen and fibrinogen degradation product deposition was membrane dependent.
the protein layer on hemodialysis membrane is a complex mixture of proteins that includes coagulation and complement factors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new technique to study the nature of the proteins deposited on hemodialyzers.
the study of the protein layer on hemodialysis hollow fiber membranes by means of a new immunohistochemical approach.
the development of a simple and reliable technique for the immunohistochemical analysis of protein deposits on dialysis membranes.

the activation of the coagulation system is the most important mechanism of protein deposition on all membranes, whereas complement activation is the major factor in the deposition of IgG and fibrinogen.
the activation of the coagulation cascade by all the membranes tested is a common phenomenon, but that the activation of complement is membrane specific.

a protein layer is deposited on the capillary wall of all hemodialysis membranes.
